2. This common order shall govern disposal of Civil Revision No.272/2019 (Munna Lal Vs.
Executive Engineer), Civil Revision No.255/2019 (Hari Singh Vs. Executive Engineer), Civil Revision No.258/2019 (Gyarsa Vs. Executive Engineer) and Civil Revision No.259/2019 (Panna Lal Vs. Executive Engineer) against order dated 12.01.2019 passed in M.J.C.No.128/2014 (New Number EX. LA 100128/2014 (Munnalal (Dead) Through LRs Vs. Executive Engineer) by First ADJ,
Begumbganj, District Raisen whereby respondents application under Section 18 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act has been allowed and petitioner references have been dismissed as time barred.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner after referring to impugned order as well as Section 18 (2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and relying upon order dated 26.03.2014 passed in Civil Revision No.430/2009 and Abhay Kumar Jain Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh AIR Online 2022 MP 2378 submits that from impugned order itself it is evident that petitioners were not present on the date of award and notice issued to them is not proper as copy of award is not proved to have been sent with the notice.

sentences.text: It is also urged that Courts below have wrongly dismissed petitioners reference by calculating limitation from the date as mentioned in certified copy of award i.e, 14.05.2013.
It is also urged that learned Courts below have erred in considering period of limitation as six weeks.

It is urged that in view of the facts of the case, period will six months from the date of knowledge of award.
4. On above grounds, it is urged that petition be allowed and impugned award be set aside.
5.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State submitted that notice under Section 12 (2) has been duly served on petitioner and petitioners have accepted award amount.
Hence, limitation period would be six weeks and not six months.
Therefore, reference Court has rightly dismissed petitioner's reference as time barred.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text:
In view of issue involved in the case, it would be appropriate to reproduce Section 18(2) of Land Acquisition Act which reads as follows:-
"(2) The application shall state the ground on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made- (a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, whichever period shall first expire."

8. Now, if impugned order is read alongwith above provision, then it is evident that reference Court has clearly held in impugned order that in view of there being no mention in the notice that copy of award was also sent.
It cannot be said that petitioner had received knowledge of award therefore, it cannot be said that notice was duly served upon petitioner under Section 12 (2) of Land Acquisition Act.
Further, it is also mentioned in the impugned order that from case file, it is clear that on the date of award, petitioner or his Advocate was not present before the Tribunal.

9. Perusal of impugned order reveal that reference Court has held that petitioner's reference is time barred on the ground that petitioner received certified copy of award on 14.05.2013 and therefore, if six weeks period is calculated from 14.05.2013, then petitioner's reference is time barred.

10. In this Court's opinion, perusal of Section 18 (2) (a) reveal that if person making the reference was present before Collector at the time of award, then applicant would have six weeks time to file reference and as per Section 18 (2) (b) in either case, period of six weeks would be available from receipt of notice under Section 12 (2).
In the instant case, both the above provisions are not applicable in view of impugned order itself and finding recorded by the reference Court.

11. In this Courts opinion, in the facts and circumstances of the case, second part of Section 18 (2)
(b) would be applicable and petitioner can file reference within six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of award i.e, 14.05.2013.

If above period of limitation is taken into consideration,
then clearly petitioner's reference is not time barred.

12. On the perusal of the application filed by respondent under Section 18 (2) of Land Acquisition Act reveal that respondent has filed above application on sole ground that award has been passed on 25.04.2009 and notice has been duly served on applicant on 02.06.2009 under Section 12.
Therefore, reference filed by the applicant is time barred.
No other ground has been taken in the application filed by respondents.
Learned Courts below had also not discussed on any other ground and has not written any finding on any other ground whatsoever.

No such ground has been taken by respondent in the application that applicant has received compensation amount therefore, they cannot file reference and this point has also not been discussed by the reference Court.

Therefore,

LA 100128/2014 (Munnalal (Dead) Through LRs Vs. Executive Engineer) are set aside and reference Court is directed to decide petitioner's reference on merits as per law.
